examples.japanese: {赤|あか}ちゃんの{洗礼式|せんれいしき}に{招待|しょうたい}された。
examples.english: I was invited to the baby's baptism ceremony.

examples.japanese: {教会|きょうかい}で{洗礼|せんれい}を{受|う}けてキリスト{教徒|きょうと}になった。
examples.english: I received baptism at a church and became a Christian.

examples.japanese: {社会|しゃかい}の{洗礼|せんれい}を{受|う}ける。
examples.english: To go through the baptism of the real world.

examples.japanese: {新人|しんじん}は{厳|きび}しい{洗礼|せんれい}を{受|う}けた。
examples.english: The newcomer went through a tough initiation.

examples.japanese: {海外|かいがい}{赴任|ふにん}の{初日|しょにち}に{文化|ぶんか}の{違|ちが}いという{洗礼|せんれい}を{浴|あ}びた。
examples.english: On my first day of the overseas posting, I was baptized by the reality of cultural differences.

notes:
Originally a Christian religious term for the sacrament of baptism. In Japanese, the figurative sense of a harsh or transformative first experience is used much more commonly than the religious sense.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {洗礼|せんれい}を{受|う}ける: to receive baptism; to undergo an initiation
- {洗礼|せんれい}を{浴|あ}びる: to be hit with an ordeal (figurative)
- {洗礼|せんれい}{名|めい}: baptismal name
- {洗礼式|せんれいしき}: baptism ceremony
- {社会|しゃかい}の{洗礼|せんれい}: the baptism of the real world

USAGE:
The figurative sense 2 is far more common in everyday Japanese. It typically describes a newcomer's difficult first encounter with something — a new job, a new environment, or harsh reality. The phrase {洗礼|せんれい}を{受|う}ける works for both senses.
